Chapter I §1.5 Lemma 1.5.1(i)-(ii) and §2.7.4 (the trace is cyclic and multiplicative)
contents.proof_mapping: cyclicity gives conjugation invariance of the ribbon trace; multiplicativity gives the trace of tensor products

contents.name: Chapter I §2.3: the category Rib_V of v-colored ribbon graphs (objects are signed colour sequences, morphisms are isotopy types, composition stacking, tensor juxtaposition) and the subcategory of colored ribbon tangles
Chapter I §2.3 Figures 2.5-2.6: the generators X^±, Y^±, Z^±, T^±, phi_V, phi'_V, d_V, dbar_V, b_V, bbar_V of Rib_V
Chapter I §2.3: ribbon tangles are ribbon graphs without coupons; the blackboard-framed cup, cap, crossing and twist are the elementary tangles
contents.proof_mapping: the evaluation functor is defined on the coupon-free subcategory, so only the tangle generators are needed

contents.name: Chapter I §2.5 Theorem I.2.5 (existence and uniqueness of the tensor functor F: Rib_V -> V with F(+)=V, F(-)=V*, F(X^+)=c, F(phi)=theta, F(b)=coev, F(d)=ev) and conditions (2.5.a)-(2.5.e)
Chapter I §2.5: isotopic ribbon graphs represent the same morphism, hence F(Omega)=F(Omega') (isotopy invariance of the operator invariant)
contents.proof_mapping: invariance of the tangle evaluation under framed isotopy is functoriality of F

contents.name: Chapter I §2.6 Corollary 2.6.1 (the double dual is canonically isomorphic to the object in a ribbon category)

Chapter I §2.7 Corollary 2.7.3 (the zero-framed Hopf link closes to tr(c c)) and the Figure 2.13-2.14 proof of cyclicity and multiplicativity
Chapter I §2.8 Corollaries 2.8.1-2.8.5 (annulus colour reversal, splitting an annulus, mirror reflection and dimensions)
contents.reason: The annulus surgery and mirror results are not consumed by any item of this pair: the pair closes braids with the pivotal trace and normalizes by the twist eigenvalue, so these transformations would add parallel machinery with no proof consumer.

contents.name: Chapter I §2.9 exercises (duality traces, framing weights of colored links, and the divisibility exercise for an annulus of color V)
contents.reason: The exercises extend the operator invariant to graphs with coupons and coloured components; the pair only needs the single-object closed-braid and tangle evaluations, and the annulus-divisibility statement is not used.

contents.name: Chapter I Lemma 3.1.1: the colored ribbon tangles X^±, Z^±, phi_V, phi'_V, b_V, d_V generate the category of colored ribbon tangles (generic Morse-position slicing argument)
Chapter I §3.2 relations (3.2.a)-(3.2.h): Yang-Baxter, cup-cap cancellation, inverse crossing and twist relations, curl-slide, and the twist-square relation
Chapter I Lemma 3.3: relations (3.2.a)-(3.2.h) are a complete set of relations between the generators of the colored ribbon tangles
Chapter I Lemma 3.4 (relations for elementary ribbon graphs with coupons, Figures 3.1-3.2)
contents.reason: The framed oriented tangle category used here is coupon-free; coupon relations would be needed only for the full v-colored ribbon-graph category Rib_V, which no item of this pair evaluates.

contents.name: Chapter I §3.5: deduction of Theorem I.2.5 from Lemmas 3.3 and 3.4 (generator values determine F, relations are checked one by one)
contents.proof_mapping: the existence half defines F on generators and checks (3.2.a)-(3.2.h), which is exactly the relation check recorded in the item strategy
